basis: Cardiac and skeletal malformations characterize this subtype; intellectual disability in 4/4 and developmental delay in 3/4 support neurologic involvement.
Craniosynostosis, nail/hair dysplasia and dental/cleft anomalies define it; sensorineural hearing loss 30-79%; intellectual disability 30-79% omitted by cap.
Primary tumour of the breast, which has no axis; sarcoma histology does not establish locomotor involvement.
Hypothalamic tumour with hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction defines the syndrome; nystagmus alone does not establish ocular damage; optic atrophy is under 30%.
Progressive leukodystrophy and thickened, hyperkeratotic skin are defining manifestations, both reported in 80-99%.
Usually arises in deep mesenchymal soft tissues of the extremities near joints; visceral primary sites and metastases do not characterize most patients.
Chronic inflammation of nasal mucosa; an infectious or allergic mechanism is not established for this umbrella concept.
Defined by a congenital atrial septal defect; the broader GATA6 association does not establish pancreatic disease in this subtype.
Defined by transient deficiency of thyroid hormones in preterm infants; no common direct injury to another organ is established.
A neurodevelopmental disorder affecting communication, social interaction and behavior; no additional organ damage defines the umbrella.
SPATA7-related retinal degeneration causes visual loss in 10/10 reported patients; no extraocular involvement is established.
Developmental disability and limb defects define it; cardiac defects and pulmonary hypoplasia each 30-79%; hearing loss, ocular and nail anomalies omitted by cap.
Defined by deficient antibody production within a syndrome; additional organ manifestations vary across subtypes and are not shared by most patients.
Pneumococcal infection directly affects the meninges; lasting hearing loss is generally below 30% overall, although rates vary by age and severity.
Ventriculomegaly in 4/4 and congenital arthrogryposis in 3/3 define the syndrome; cerebellar hypoplasia further supports neurologic involvement.
Adenoma arises in extrahepatic bile ducts, which belong to the hepatic axis.
Malignant tumour originates in the central nervous system; fibroblastic histology does not establish musculoskeletal involvement.
Inflammation affects ethmoid sinus mucosa, an upper airway site; the definition does not establish bone injury or a specific infectious mechanism.
Defined by long-bone diaphyseal sclerosis; a small study's cardiac association does not establish common direct cardiac involvement.
Impacted gallstones cause extrahepatic biliary obstruction; gallbladder and bile ducts are hepatic. Pancreatitis occurs in only 5-29%.
A benign peripheral nerve sheath tumour defined by increased cellularity; no specific cutaneous location is established.
Inherited defects of hepatic bilirubin processing define this metabolic umbrella; neurologic injury is confined to severe subtypes rather than most patients.
Cardiac defects, clubfoot and Robin/cleft palate define it; neurodevelopmental impairment 30-79%; hepatic failure reported in 1/2, omitted by cap.
Cowden mucocutaneous and GI hamartomas define it; benign thyroid lesions occur in roughly 50-70% of Cowden patients, with limited subtype data; ID is 12%.
Congenital narrowing of the tricuspid valve defines the disease; regurgitation and heart failure remain within the cardiovascular axis.
